name: run-error-first-admitted
description: ADMITTED GAP — admission is right, surfacing is not: a stream may open with RUN_ERROR (the spec admits it because a run can fail before it begins) and the client does admit it rather than raising a first-event violation; but a producer-sent RUN_ERROR never reaches the caller as a failure — runAgent() resolves — so the `failed` outcome the fixture format defines as covering a producer-sent RUN_ERROR is not observable. This pins both halves so neither can change unnoticed
kill: narrow the first-event check in verifyEvents (`eventType !== RUN_STARTED && eventType !== RUN_ERROR`) to RUN_STARTED alone — the leading RUN_ERROR then fails with `First event must be 'RUN_STARTED'` and this fixture's completed outcome fails. The second half is a gap, not a rule: making a producer-sent RUN_ERROR reject the run is the RIGHT fix, and it makes this fixture fail too. Anyone landing that MUST flip this fixture and late-run-error-after-finished-admitted to `failed` + `errorContains` in the same change.
